usual_baseline: Debridement within 24 h is usually met: 98.8% [1325], 81% [1464]. Time-critical items are poor. Antibiotics within 1 hour were 41.7% [1383] and 27% [1402]. High-energy debridement within 12 h was 41.7% [1383] and 25% [1464]. Soft tissue cover within 72 h was 56.4% [1325] and 27% [1402]. Full BOAST compliance was 8.8% [1482].
fix_that_works: Tracking antibiotic order and administration times with quarterly audits significantly improved antibiotics within 1 hour [1379]. A microlearning video after an infographic cut unnecessary antibiotics for open hand injuries from 50.0% to 14.3% (p=0.002) [1474]. Unspecified practice changes raised soft tissue cover within 5 days from 50% to all patients [1186].
fix_that_fails: Education alone did not improve antibiotic timing [1379]. An infographic poster alone left unnecessary antibiotics at 43.8%, not significant [1474]. Antibiotic choice was not audited against a fix: 59.3% received a regimen outside the protocol, and only 14.1% had tetanus immunisation [1370].
consultant_advice: Single-site BOAST 4 compliance audits are common, and they rarely close the loop. Choose one time-critical measure, such as antibiotics within 1 hour or 72-hour soft tissue cover. Track it with timestamps, and link it to infection rates, which were 13% [1464] and 24% [1482].
